content.text:
Fenwick is now an operator at level 4 (full admin), and the server is back up and responding.

**One thing I had to fix:** your server runs in offline mode (`online-mode=false`), so it identifies players by an ID worked out from their username, not their Mojang account ID. When I ran the op command, it recorded Fenwick's Mojang account ID, so the op wouldn't have applied when he joined. I swapped in the correct offline ID, checked the method against Marigold42's existing entry, and restarted the server. Restarting was the only way to make it load the corrected file. Fenwick will have op rights next time he logs in.

**A security note:** in offline mode the server doesn't check who anyone really is. Anyone who sets their username to "Fenwick" will be treated as him. Ops also skip the whitelist, so that person could get in and have full admin powers even though Fenwick isn't on the whitelist. If your players all use official Minecraft accounts, I'd recommend turning on online mode. That change would mean updating the existing op and whitelist entries to match. Let me know if you want me to do that, or if you'd like Fenwick at a lower op level (for example, level 2 lets him use gameplay commands without server-management powers).
